newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds tumble at close, underperform U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds tumble at close, underperform U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much weaker on Wednesday, underperforming U.S. bonds, as currency weakness, new supply, and profit taking on Canada-U.S. spread narrowing trades sent the market tumbling, dealers said.

"It's a combination of weakness from the States, a weak Canadian dollar, and belief that spread compression may have run its course for the time being," said Michael Gregory, an economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.35 to C$114.25 to yield 6.829 percent against the U.S. 30-year bonds, which fell 12/32 to yield 6.39 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 44 basis points from 36 basis points at Tuesday's close.

The Canadian dollar weakened to its lowest point in more than a month today, at one point softening past C$1.3540 (US$0.7385) from its open at C$1.3511 (US$0.7401). The weaker currency has made further rate cuts by the Bank of Canada unlikely and prompted many investors to take profits on spread narrowing between Canadian and U.S. bonds, analysts said.
"The market was priced for further potential rate cuts, but the currency has done it for itself," said one trader. "There's been supply and no customers to buy it."

The Bank of Canada measures the level of easing or tightening of monetary conditions in Canada using the monetary conditions index, which is calculated using short-term interest rates and the currency. With the weakness in the dollar, the MCI as calculated by Reuters today reached its lowest point this year, making another rate cut unlikely.
Dealers said today's price moves were exaggerated to some degree by thinner-than-usual volumes in the market.
"We're not seeing huge, massive volumes of selling here by any means," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc.

In auction news, the Government of Canada's auction of C$3 billion of 4.0 percent bonds due 1999 produced an average yield of 4.012 percent, with a high yield of 4.023 percent and a low yield of 4.0 percent.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$1.22 to C$105.80 to yield 6.211 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.11 percent.
The spread between the bonds moved to a positive 10 basis points from a negative spread of one basis point.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.83 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.02 percent.
